features.definition: Access, extract, and reshape deeply-nested target objects using declarative spec primitives (such as Path, Spec, T, Coalesce, Call, Invoke, and Ref) with fallback handling, target-relative expressions, and explicit exception management.
features.name: Core Specification and Path-Based Navigation

features.definition: Perform in-place deep assignments and deep deletions across nested data structures and custom object hierarchies based on glom paths.
features.name: Target Mutation and In-Place Operations

features.definition: Validate, assert, and conditionally route target data structures using specifiers such as Match, Check, Switch, Regex, and logical combinators (And, Or, Not).
features.name: Pattern Matching and Data Validation

features.definition: Group, partition, and bucket iterable target data into hierarchical buckets and compute aggregate summaries using accumulators like First, Avg, Max, Min, and Sample.
features.name: Data Grouping, Aggregation, and Bucketing

features.definition: Fold and aggregate iterable datasets through custom reducers, summation, counting, and list or collection flattening operations.
features.name: Reductions, Merging, and Flattening

features.definition: Process and transform iterable data streams lazily using operations such as map, filter, chunked, windowed, split, flatten, unique, slice, takewhile, dropwhile, and terminal evaluations.
features.name: Lazy Streaming Pipelines

features.definition: Run glom transformations and queries directly from the terminal or shell pipelines against various data formats (JSON, Python, TOML, YAML) provided via arguments, files, or standard input.
features.name: Command-Line Interface (CLI)

project_purpose: glom is a Python library and CLI tool for declarative nested data access, mutation, restructuring, and validation. It lets developers navigate and transform complex, deeply-nested Python objects and serialized formats using composable, expressive specifications with detailed error handling.
